moments.title: Calm before the storm
moments.context: ES has climbed slowly for two weeks with small, quiet candles. Nothing on the calendar looks scary.
moments.story: Friday 10 Oct: President Trump threatened a "massive increase" in tariffs on Chinese imports. ES fell 2.71% in a single day, the S&P 500's worst day since April. Within two weeks it had recovered and made new highs.
moments.lesson: Quiet trends can end without warning. That's why every trade needs a stop, even when the chart looks calm.

moments.title: Nvidia reports tonight
moments.context: ES has pulled back 4.2% from its October high and is below the blue average. Nvidia, the biggest AI stock, reports earnings after the close.
moments.story: Nvidia beat expectations and ES opened higher, but the rally reversed and Thursday closed 1.56% lower, at the day's low. On Friday the New York Fed's John Williams hinted at a rate cut, buyers came back, and by early December ES was close to its highs again.
moments.lesson: News moves price, but not always the way you'd guess. Watch how the chart reacts to news, not the headline itself.

moments.title: Good news, red candle
moments.context: Today ES opened higher on Nvidia's strong earnings, then fell all day and closed right at its low.
moments.story: No follow-through. Friday dipped only 26 points lower, then the New York Fed hinted at a rate cut and ES closed 0.96% higher. It kept rallying for two weeks.
moments.lesson: A scary candle that gets no follow-through often marks the low. Wait for the next session to confirm before chasing.

moments.title: Poking the ceiling
moments.context: ES has been stuck between about 6,814 and 7,040 for five weeks. Today it poked above 7,040 but closed back below it.
moments.story: The breakout failed. ES drifted back to the bottom of the range within a week (low 6,785.00 on 5 Feb).
moments.lesson: In a sideways range, a poke above the ceiling that closes back inside is a warning, not a breakout.

moments.title: Through the floor?
moments.context: ES just dipped below the bottom of its five-week sideways range.
moments.story: Friday ran the stop orders under the floor, then closed 1.94% higher, straight back inside the range. A classic false breakdown.
moments.lesson: Obvious lows attract stop orders. When those get cleared and no new sellers appear, price snaps back.

moments.title: War sell-off
moments.context: A month after US–Israeli strikes on Iran began, ES has fallen about 8% and sits far below its averages. Today closed near the low.
moments.story: Monday made one last marginal low, then Tuesday 31 Mar jumped 2.86%. When a two-week ceasefire was announced on 7 Apr, the rebound turned into a V-shaped recovery.
moments.lesson: When price is stretched far below its average, selling late is risky. Snapback rallies are violent.

moments.title: Deadline night
moments.context: President Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz expires tonight. ES has made higher lows for a week under a ceiling near 6,675.
moments.story: A two-week ceasefire was announced less than two hours before the deadline. ES jumped 2.51% the next day and kept climbing for weeks.
moments.lesson: Before big yes/no events, keep your size small. The gap can go either way and blow straight past a stop.

moments.title: Nine weeks up
moments.context: The S&P 500 has risen nine weeks in a row. Tomorrow morning brings the monthly US jobs report.
moments.story: A hotter-than-expected jobs report raised fears of a Fed rate hike and chip stocks crashed. ES fell 2.64% on Friday, then whipsawed for a week before recovering.
moments.lesson: Long winning streaks make traders complacent right before volatility returns.

moments.title: Breakdown or trap?
moments.context: ES just broke below the floor of a month-long sideways range and closed near the low.
moments.story: The next day ES opened near its low and closed 1.65% higher, back inside the range. Trapped sellers had to buy back, and within two weeks ES was above the top of the range.
moments.lesson: A breakdown that's reversed the very next day is a trap. Failed moves often run hard the other way.

moments.title: Dip in a strong trend
moments.context: The Nasdaq-100 has rallied about 26% from its late-March low without closing below its blue average once. This is the third down day in a row.
moments.story: The dip held above the average. NQ rose 1.61% the next day and made new highs within a week.
moments.lesson: In strong uptrends, short dips usually get bought. Fighting a strong trend is expensive.

moments.title: Six days down
moments.context: NQ has closed lower six days in a row, is down 9.0% in three weeks, and sits far below its blue average.
moments.story: Thursday opened at its exact low of the day and closed 3.28% higher. Two and a half weeks later NQ had recovered the entire decline.
moments.lesson: After long losing streaks far below the average, sellers run out of steam. That's a dangerous place to start a short.

moments.title: First red day at the top
moments.context: NQ has fully recovered its July drop and is near its highs. Today was the first big red candle in nearly three weeks.
moments.story: The red candle was the start of a pause, not a crash. NQ chopped sideways in a range for the next three weeks.
moments.lesson: One red candle at the top doesn't make a downtrend. Without lower highs and lower lows, it's just a pause.

moments.title: Friday before the strikes
moments.context: Crude oil has drifted higher for six weeks. It's the Friday close, and markets shut for the weekend.
moments.story: On Saturday the US and Israel struck Iran. Crude opened Monday $7.98 higher, straight past any nearby stop, and a week later it was up 35.6%.
moments.lesson: Weekend news can gap price far past your stop. Position size, not the stop, is your real protection.

moments.title: Oil goes vertical
moments.context: Crude has jumped from $67.02 to $90.90 in a week as the Iran war disrupts Gulf supplies.
moments.story: Monday spiked to $119.48 overnight, then crashed back to close at $94.77. Tuesday fell another 11.9%. That spike high was never seen again in this data.
moments.lesson: Parabolic moves end in wild volatility. The later you join, the worse your risk.

moments.title: The $119 spike
moments.context: Crude spiked to $119.48 overnight, crashed to $81.19, and closed at $94.77: a huge candle with long wicks on both ends.
moments.story: Tuesday crude fell another 11.9%, then swung wildly back up. Later in March it was above $100 again, but the spike high held.
moments.lesson: Huge candles with long wicks on both sides show a market that can't agree on price. Expect big swings both ways.

moments.title: Deadline night (oil)
moments.context: Crude is back above $110. The deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz expires tonight.
moments.story: A ceasefire was announced just before the deadline, with tankers allowed through Hormuz. Crude fell 16.4% the next day.
moments.lesson: One headline can move crude more than a month of normal trading. Size every trade for the gap.

moments.title: Bounce into the average
moments.context: Crude has been falling since late April. This three-day bounce has just reached the falling blue average.
moments.story: The bounce failed right at the average. Crude fell 20% over the next two weeks.
moments.lesson: In a downtrend, rallies up to the falling average are where sellers come back.

moments.title: Quiet after the fall
moments.context: After falling more than 30%, crude has gone sideways between about $67.04 and $73.18 for two weeks, with shrinking daily moves.
moments.story: The quiet ended with a breakout: crude jumped 9.4% on 13 Jul and kept rising.
moments.lesson: After a big fall, quiet sideways trading (a base) often comes before the next big move up.

moments.title: Gold goes parabolic
moments.context: Gold is up 22% this month to a record above $5,303.60, and the climb keeps getting steeper. It's far above its blue average.
moments.story: One more record the next day ($5,586.20), then on 30 Jan President Trump picked Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair. The dollar jumped and gold fell 10.8% in a day, one of its worst days in decades.
moments.lesson: The steeper a rally gets, the harder it can fall, and the wilder the swings get. Here even a correct sell was stopped out by the final spike first. In parabolic markets, staying out is often the smart trade.

moments.title: A wild record day
moments.context: Gold hit a record $5,586.20 today, then swung $488.70 and closed below where it opened.
moments.story: The next day the Warsh nomination hit and gold collapsed 10.8%. Two sessions after the record it was 20.8% lower.
moments.lesson: A huge-range day at a record high warns that the rally's fuel is running out.

moments.title: After the crash
moments.context: Gold has fallen about 21% from its record in two days, back to early-January prices, but closed well off today's low.
moments.story: Gold jumped 6.1% the next day and kept climbing for weeks.
moments.lesson: After a crash, old price zones where buyers were active often attract buyers again.

moments.title: The coil
moments.context: Gold has been stuck between about $3,955.40 and $4,215.50 for six weeks, and its daily moves keep shrinking.
moments.story: Gold broke out the next day with a 3.7% jump and ran to $4,755.00 by late August.
moments.lesson: Shrinking daily moves inside a range are energy building up. The breakout often comes suddenly.

moments.title: Weaker and weaker rallies
moments.context: Since its late-August peak, each gold rally has stopped lower than the last, while support near $4,273.30 keeps holding.
moments.story: Support broke on Monday 28 Sep with a 3.5% drop, and gold kept sliding through October.
moments.lesson: Falling highs pressing on flat support usually break downward.

moments.title: Everyone is short
moments.context: Bitcoin has bounced from $29,209 (20 Jul) to $35,412, up five days in a row. It is still far below its spring highs, and many traders are betting on another leg down.
moments.story: Monday 26 Jul: a newspaper report said Amazon would soon accept bitcoin (Amazon denied it). BTC spiked to $40,567 as traders who had bet on a fall were forced to buy back, a classic short squeeze. By 30 Jul it closed at $42,218.
moments.lesson: When most traders lean one way, a small spark can force a violent move the other way. A trend that starts with a squeeze often keeps going.

moments.title: Bitcoin becomes money
moments.context: BTC has climbed from under $30k in July to $52,687, closing higher on 6 of the last 7 days. Tomorrow El Salvador makes bitcoin legal tender, a first for any country.
moments.story: 7 Sep: instead of a celebration, BTC crashed from $52,944 to $42,069 within hours as over-leveraged buyers were liquidated. It closed the day 11.1% lower at $46,839, and two weeks later it was lower still at $43,014.
moments.lesson: "Buy the rumour, sell the news." When a famous event arrives after a long rally, the good news is usually already in the price.

moments.title: A record on ETF day
moments.context: The first US bitcoin futures ETF started trading yesterday. Today BTC hit a record $67,145 and closed at $66,037, up about 60% in a month.
moments.story: The next day BTC fell 5.8% and by 27 Oct it had dropped to $57,960. It took until November to reclaim the high.
moments.lesson: Big headline days often mark short-term tops. After a vertical run, the first heavy red candle is the warning that buyers are exhausted.

moments.title: Breakout to a new record
moments.context: BTC jumped 6.7% to a record close of $67,598 yesterday and held near the highs today. US inflation figures come out tomorrow.
moments.story: 10 Nov: US inflation came in at 6.2%, the highest in over 30 years. BTC spiked to $69,127, then reversed to close at $64,893. That spike stayed bitcoin's all-time high until March 2024. Within two weeks BTC was down at $55,230.
moments.lesson: A record high that closes well off its top shows buyers could not hold the breakout. Records are where profit-taking clusters.

moments.title: Friday night, falling knife
moments.context: BTC has slid from its $69k record to $53,681. Today alone it fell 5.0%, with a low of $49,569, and it is well below the blue average. Weekend markets are thin.
moments.story: Early Saturday 4 Dec BTC collapsed to $41,035 in a few hours as leveraged buyers were force-sold, then bounced to close at $49,218. Over the next two weeks it never closed above $51,000.
moments.lesson: Below a falling average, drops can accelerate when leverage unwinds, and thin weekend markets make moves extreme. Rallies inside a downtrend get sold.

moments.title: War fears
moments.context: BTC has slid from $44,589 to $37,257 in a week as tension over Ukraine grows.
moments.story: 24 Feb: Russia invaded Ukraine. BTC dropped to $34,348 within hours, then buyers stepped in and it closed 2.9% higher at $38,337, leaving a long lower wick. On 28 Feb it jumped 14.6%.
moments.lesson: When the feared event finally happens, much of the selling is already done. A long lower wick on huge news shows sellers ran out of steam.

moments.title: The stablecoin cracks
moments.context: BTC has fallen four days in a row to $34,059, its lowest close since July 2021. TerraUSD (UST), one of the biggest "stablecoins" meant to stay at $1, slipped below its peg this weekend.
moments.story: UST never recovered: it and its sister coin LUNA collapsed to almost nothing, and Terra's reserve sold its bitcoin trying to defend the peg. BTC fell 11.7% on 9 May and hit $25,259 on 12 May, its lowest since December 2020.
moments.lesson: Forced sellers don't care about price. When a big holder must sell, the selling feeds itself and a downtrend runs further than anyone expects.

moments.title: Six red days
moments.context: BTC has closed lower six days in a row, from $31,353 to $26,568, after US inflation hit 8.6% on Friday, a 40-year high.
moments.story: Hours later, crypto lender Celsius froze customer withdrawals. BTC fell 15.5% on 13 June. On 15 June the Fed raised rates by 0.75%, its biggest hike since 1994, and on 18 June BTC hit $17,568.
moments.lesson: Six red days below a falling average is a downtrend, not a bargain. "It has already fallen a lot" is not a reason to buy.

moments.title: Rally into inflation day
moments.context: BTC jumped 10.6% on Friday and has closed higher six days in a row, now at $22,391. US inflation numbers come out tomorrow, and traders hope they will show inflation cooling.
moments.story: 13 Sep: inflation came in hotter than expected (8.3%). US stocks had their worst day since June 2020 and BTC fell 9.9% in one candle, wiping out the rally. A week later it closed below $19,000.
moments.lesson: A rally into a big scheduled number is a bet on that number. One candle can erase a week, so size every trade so a single candle can't hurt you badly.

moments.title: Trouble at FTX
moments.context: BTC has been unusually calm for weeks, between about $18k and $21.5k, and closed at $20,581. Over the weekend the boss of Binance said it would sell its FTT tokens, the token of rival exchange FTX, raising questions about FTX's finances.
moments.story: 8 Nov: FTX stopped customer withdrawals. Binance agreed to rescue it, then walked away the next day, and FTX filed for bankruptcy on 11 Nov. BTC fell 10.0% and then 14.7%, hitting $15,439, its lowest since November 2020.
moments.lesson: Long, quiet ranges end with big moves. A tight range tells you a move is coming, not which way. That's what stops are for.

moments.title: New low, maximum fear
moments.context: BTC just made a new low at $15,412 after the FTX collapse. It is 77% below its 2021 record and sentiment could hardly be worse.
moments.story: This turned out to be the low of the 2022 bear market. BTC crept back to $17,245 by 30 Nov and, after a quiet December, rallied above $23,000 in January 2023.
moments.lesson: Bottoms are only obvious afterwards. Watch what happens next: when new lows stop making progress, sellers are running out. Waiting for that confirmation is safer than guessing the exact low.

moments.title: Seven quiet weeks
moments.context: BTC has barely moved for seven weeks, roughly between $16,000 and $18,400. Today it closed at $17,951, its highest close since 8 Nov. US inflation data comes out tomorrow.
moments.story: 12 Jan: inflation fell to 6.5%, the sixth monthly drop in a row. BTC rose 5.0% that day and kept going: $20,966 by 14 Jan and $22,676 by 20 Jan, up 26% in nine days.
moments.lesson: The longer a market goes sideways, the bigger the move when it finally breaks. A close at the top of a long range is an early clue.

moments.title: Banks are failing
moments.context: Crypto-friendly Silvergate Bank said on Wednesday it would shut down, and today US regulators seized Silicon Valley Bank. BTC has fallen from $22,192 to $20,207 in three days.
moments.story: Over the weekend the USDC stablecoin lost its $1 peg after its issuer revealed $3.3 billion stuck at SVB. On Sunday night US authorities guaranteed all SVB deposits. BTC rose 7.5% on 12 Mar and 9.0% on 13 Mar, hit $26,601 on 14 Mar and closed above $28,000 on 19 Mar.
moments.lesson: When panic peaks and its cause is removed, traders who sold or shorted rush back in and price can rip higher. Selling after a big drop into extreme fear has poor odds.
